findings.where: Step 7 (A smaller rate) text, used by steps 8, 11 and 12
findings.what: The screen jumps from 'a twentieth of a year at 100%' to 'e^0.05' without writing e^(1/20) = e^0.05, and no screen says why t years at rate k give e^(kt) (t years at 5% are t/20 years at 100%, or (e^k)^t = e^(kt) by the power law from Powers and roots), so step 8 hands over e^(0.05t) and step 11's 'multiply the rate by the time' arrive as a rule; one sentence here closes both gaps.

It says 'after t years it is eᵗ' and then uses half a year, e^0.5, without the one clause that makes a fraction of a year work (two half-years make a year, so each half multiplies by e^0.5, the number that times itself gives e), and step 7's twentieth-of-a-year argument rests on that clause.

It says 365 to 8,760 parts 'adds only about 36p, from £271.46 to £271.81', but the two figures shown differ by 35p (36p comes from the unrounded 35.6p), so a hand check against the screen comes out 1p short; say 'about 35p'.

findings.where: SVG labels on steps 5, 7, 8, 9 and 10 (marks 'e^0.5 ≈ 1.6487', rate row 'never pausing, e^0.05', keys 'e^(0.05t)', 'e^(−t)', '400 e^(−0.1t) volts')
findings.what: The picture writes powers with a caret while the words directly above raise them, so one screen shows two notations for the same thing; raise the power in the SVG text too (a tspan with a dy shift and smaller size).

'At every point its slope equals its height' drops the verified lesson's 'textbooks add' label, but the tracker only measures it from x = 0 to 2; keep the label or say 'at every point you slide to'. Also, 'Slide the point along the curve' invites a drag on the ring, but only the track below moves it.

£271.81 is the only exact figure beside 'Without limit' and 'About £300', so the guess-first screen can be won from precision rather than from the table's shrinking gaps; give the distractors exact values too.

At the opening 5% the four bars measure 97.5% to 100% of one width and look identical, so nothing visibly settles until he slides; tell him to try 100%, where the 1-part bar stops at 58% of the never-pausing one, or let the demonstration sweep the rate once.
